s: with (in the company of, alongside)
Ich spiele mit meinen Freunden.
I'm playing with my friends.
with, by (using as an instrument, by means of)
Ich schreibe mit einem Bleistift.
I'm writing with a pencil.
Ich fahre mit dem Bus.
I'm going by bus.
with (having a property, accessory or possession)
Siehst du den Mann mit der Brille da drüben?
Do you see the man with the glasses over there?
Mit ausreichend Übung passiert dir das nicht mehr.
With enough practice, that won't happen to you anymore.
with (having a property, accessory or possession): including, with ... included
with (having a property, accessory or possession): at (with the age of)
Er hat mit fünf Jahren lesen gelernt.
He learned how to read at five years old.
with, at (coinciding with a specific condition or event)
Diese Tiere werden nur mit Einbruch der Dämmerung aktiv.
These animals only become active at the break of dawn/start of dusk.
with, at (coinciding with a specific condition or event): with (accompanied by a certain behavior)
Er stürzte sich mit einem wilden Schrei auf ihn.
He flung himself at him with a savage yell.
with, at (coinciding with a specific condition or event): Used to describe the current activity or occupation with certain verbs.
mit etwas anfangen
to start doing something, to start with something (out of multiple options)
mit etwas aufhören
to stop doing something
regarding, having to do with
informal
Was ist mit mir?
What about me?
Das mit dem Beschwerdebrief sollten wir uns nochmal überlegen.
The thing with the complaint letter, we should maybe think that over.
mit.et: From Middle High German mite, mit, from Old High German miti, mit, from Proto-West Germanic *midi. Cognate with German Low German met, mihe- (separable part of verbs) (Paderbornisch) and Middle English mid (“with”).

s: among; denotes a belonging of a person or a thing to a group
Hier gibt es mit das beste Essen in der Stadt.
Here they have some of the best food in town.
Ich war mit der erste, der hier war.
I was one of the very first who arrived.
also, too (in addition; besides; as well)
with (something), with it
informal
Ich brauch nicht unbedingt Mayonnaise zu den Fritten, aber mit sind sie natürlich besser.
I don't necessarily need mayonnaise with the chips, but they taste better with it, of course.
mit.et: From Middle High German mite, mit, from Old High German miti, mit, from Proto-West Germanic *midi. Cognate with German Low German met, mihe- (separable part of verbs) (Paderbornisch) and Middle English mid (“with”).

s: a prefix of nearly unlimited productivity, expressing that something is done together with others who do the same thing, sometimes equivalent to English co- or along.
mit- + tanzen (“to dance”) → mittanzen (“to dance with others, to join others in dancing, to dance along”)
co-, fellow
mit- + Verschwörer (“conspirator”) → Mitverschwörer (“co-conspirator”)
mit- + Bürger (“citizen”) → Mitbürger (“fellow citizen”)
mit-.et: From mit (“with”). Compare Dutch mee-, mede-.
